hints.content:
We can map a figure onto a **similar** figure using only rigid transformations and dilations. This means the figures must have exactly the same shapes, but may have different sizes.

For triangles in particular, two triangles are similar if all of their corresponding angles are [[☃ definition 1]].

options.definition: Angles with the same measure that we can map onto each other using rigid transformations

hints.content:
Triangle $ABC$ has angle measures of $57^\circ$ and $44^\circ$. The third angle measure is therefore $180^\circ - 57^\circ - 44^\circ = 79^\circ$.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: Triangle A B C. Angle A is forty-four degrees. Angle B is fifty-seven degrees. Angle C is seventy-nine degrees.

hints.content:
Triangle $GHI$ has angle measures of $44^\circ$ and $79^\circ$. The third angle measure is $180^\circ - 44^\circ - 79^\circ = 57^\circ$. 



[[☃ image 1]]

Therefore $\triangle GHI$ is similar to $\triangle ABC$.

options.alt: Triangle G H I. Angle G is forty-four degrees. Angle H is fifty-seven degrees. Angle I is seventy-nine degrees.

hints.content:
Triangle $JKL$ has angle measures of $57^\circ$ and $44^\circ$. The third angle measure is $180^\circ - 57^\circ - 44^\circ = 79^\circ$.



[[☃ image 1]]

Therefore $\triangle JKL$ is similar to $\triangle ABC$.

options.alt: Triangle J K L. Angle L is forty-four degrees. Angle K is fifty-seven degrees. Angle J is seventy-nine degrees.

hints.content: In conclusion, *both* triangles are similar to $\triangle ABC$.
